fi-serranus-tortugarum.title: Chalk Bass
fi-serranus-tortugarum.summary: A small, hardy Caribbean bass with orange, lavender and blue bands. Good for beginners and reef tanks.
rows: About 3 in; wild record 8 cm (3.1 in) TL (FishBase)
Several can share a tank if all are added at the same time
Yes. Ignores corals, but larger fish may eat small shrimp
Western Atlantic: southern Florida (USA), Bahamas, Honduras and Virgin Islands; probably widespread in Caribbean reef areas
notes: Give it live rock to hide in.
Hovers over rubble in small groups in the wild.

fi-serranus-tigrinus.title: Harlequin Bass
fi-serranus-tigrinus.summary: A very hardy Caribbean bass with bold black, white and yellow mottling. As it grows it will eat smaller fish and crustaceans.
rows: About 11.5 in; wild record 29 cm (11.4 in) FL (FishBase)
With caution. Safe with corals, but small fish and shrimp become food as it grows
Carnivore. Meaty foods; wild fish eat mostly crustaceans
Western Atlantic: Bermuda and southern Florida, USA to northern South America; throughout the Caribbean
notes: Wants plenty of caves and a 75 gal or larger tank.

fi-serranus-baldwini.title: Lantern Bass
fi-serranus-baldwini.summary: A small, disease-resistant Caribbean bass with orange, black and brown markings.
rows: About 4.5 in; wild record 12 cm (4.7 in) TL (FishBase)
More than one can be kept if added together
With caution. Leaves corals alone but will eat small shrimp and very small fish
Carnivore. Meaty foods; in the wild it eats small shrimp and fish
Western Atlantic: southern Florida, USA and Bahamas to southeastern Brazil
notes: Wants plenty of live rock for cover.

fi-gramma-loreto.title: Royal Gramma
fi-gramma-loreto.summary: A purple-and-yellow Caribbean basslet that stays small and is a classic beginner reef fish.
rows: About 3 in; wild record 8 cm (3.1 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep one; it is territorial toward its own kind
Carnivore. Mysis, brine shrimp and other frozen meaty foods
Western Central Atlantic: Bermuda, Bahamas, and Central America to northern South America
notes: Likes caves and overhangs, and often swims upside down under ledges.

fi-serranus-tabacarius.title: Tobacco Bass
fi-serranus-tabacarius.summary: A hardy Western Atlantic bass with an orange band splitting a gray belly from a mottled back.
rows: About 7 in; wild record 22 cm (8.7 in) TL (FishBase)
If keeping more than one, add them together
With caution. Bigger fish may eat small crustaceans and tiny fish
Western Atlantic: Bermuda and southern Florida, USA to northern Brazil
notes: Best in a fish-only tank, or a reef without small shrimp, gobies or blennies.

fi-gramma-melacara.title: Blackcap Basslet
fi-gramma-melacara.summary: A small purple basslet with a black "cap" from deeper outer reef walls and overhangs in the Caribbean and Bahamas. Shy and cover-loving, and a good reef fish.
rows: About 4 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 10 cm (3.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: mysis shrimp, enriched brine shrimp, chopped krill, chopped marine fish flesh, clam, chopped seafood, small marine pellets
Western Central Atlantic: West Indies including the Bahamas and Central America
notes: Give it caves and overhangs; avoid aggressive damsels and pushy wrasses.

fi-assessor-macneilli.title: Blue Assessor (MacNeill's Assessor)
fi-assessor-macneilli.summary: A small, dusky navy-blue basslet with electric-blue fin edges. In the wild it gathers in caves, often swimming upside down. A good reef fish.
rows: About 3 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 6 cm (2.4 in) TL (FishBase)
One per tank (or one male); it is territorial with its own kind
Carnivore: meaty foods such as mysis, enriched brine shrimp, finely chopped seafood and frozen carnivore mixes, at least twice a day
Western Pacific: Great Barrier Reef in Australia and New Caledonia
notes: Give plenty of rock caves. Corals and larger shrimp are safe, though tiny pods may be eaten.
Males brood the eggs in their mouths.

fi-pseudochromis-diadema.title: Diadem Dottyback
fi-pseudochromis-diadema.summary: A bright yellow dottyback with a purple-magenta stripe running from its head along the back, from the Western Pacific. Colorful and easy, but pushy for its size.
rows: About 3 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 6.2 cm (2.4 in) TL (FishBase)
One per tank unless the tank is large and heavily aquascaped
Carnivore: frozen mysis and brine shrimp, marine pellets and flake; it will also hunt bristleworms
Western Central Pacific: Peninsular Malaysia, the Philippines and northern Borneo
notes: Build rockwork with lots of caves and crevices so it can claim a home.
A known jumper: keep a tight-fitting lid.
FishBase now files it as Pictichromis diadema.
